name: dr-tourism-dashboard
what_it_holds: Single-file static HTML dashboard (index.html, ~37KB, one commit, updated 2026-05-30) with embedded (hand-entered, not linked raw files) Dominican Republic tourism series 2019-2025: total visitor arrivals (6.4M in 2019 to 12.5M 2025e), air arrivals, cruise passengers (1.1M to 2.65M), tourism revenue in USD ($7.5B to $10.9B), tourism as % of GDP (8.1% to 8.8%), 2024 airport-level passenger counts (Punta Cana 9.55M, Las Americas 5.48M, Cibao 2.29M, Puerto Plata with 2021-2024 breakdown), 2024 source-market shares (USA 50%, Canada 12%, Panama 6%, Colombia 5%, Puerto Rico 5%), and hotel room capacity (87,322 rooms, 10,060 pipeline). Footer cites sources: MITUR, JAC, Banco Central (BCRD), ASONAHORES, UN Tourism.
why_useful: Directly addresses gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, specifically Caribbean/LatAm) with a compact, already-aggregated annual DR tourism series through 2024/2025 sourced from BCRD/MITUR — useful as a cross-check series or to locate the underlying BCRD/MITUR releases, though the repo itself is a single static page with numbers baked into HTML, not a machine-readable table, and it is a personal project (0 stars) so the figures are unverified against source.
themes: Caribbean, Central America and island tourism stats (CTO, Costa Rica ICT, Dominican Republic BCRD, Bahamas, Puerto Rico) and Hawaii-like party-size / length-of-stay surveys
why_all: Directly addresses gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, specifically Caribbean/LatAm) with a compact, already-aggregated annual DR tourism series through 2024/2025 sourced from BCRD/MITUR — useful as a cross-check series or to locate the underlying BCRD/MITUR releases, though the repo itself is a single static page with numbers baked into HTML, not a machine-readable table, and it is a personal project (0 stars) so the figures are unverified against source.

If the embedded numbers do trace to BCRD's published monthly visitor-arrival series, this would be a quick pointer to DR travel-volume data (gap #7 region), but the single-file, single-commit shape and lack of source documentation makes this unverified — flagging for a human to open the HTML and check whether it cites real BCRD figures.

name: hawaii-tourism-los-calculator
what_it_holds: Web app (importData.js loads a CSV into MongoDB) built around the same 'Hawaii Tourism Data (from DBEDT Data Warehouse)' source (1999-2021) as the danielnaqvi repo above; computes min/max average length-of-stay by visitor category and location/island. Raw CSV file is referenced by name but not clearly persisted in git (loaded into a database instead), so treat as a method/app rather than a guaranteed data mirror.
why_useful: Second independent implementation over the same DBEDT length-of-stay dataset; useful mainly as confirmation the dataset exists and as an alternate ingestion script if the danielnaqvi CSV is incomplete.
